claims.text: Fixed high laser-power and scan-speed settings for L-PBF of AlCrFeNiSi produce steep thermal gradients.
Rapid thermal cycles and steep thermal gradients cause residual stresses and microstructural inhomogeneities in AlCrFeNiSi.
A real-time machine-learning controller will use in-situ thermal feedback to modulate laser power and scan speed during L-PBF.
Dynamic laser-parameter adjustment changes melt-pool size and cooling rate.
Adaptive parameter adjustment produces a more uniform thermal profile during solidification.
A more uniform thermal profile minimizes the formation of large columnar grains.
Large columnar grains are associated with hot-cracking susceptibility and residual-stress concentrations.
The machine-learning algorithm will continuously analyze melt-pool thermal images and adjust process parameters in real time.
Lowering peak temperatures and smoothing cooling rates reduce thermal shock and intergranular stress.
Reducing thermal load lowers hot-cracking tendencies.
Adaptive thermal control promotes a finer and more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Adaptive processing will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to fixed-parameter high-thermal-load processing.
Adaptive processing will produce a finer and more uniform microstructure than fixed-parameter processing.
Adaptive processing will improve tensile strength and ductility relative to fixed-parameter processing.
Conventional fixed high-power and high-scan-speed L-PBF produces high residual stresses and microstructural defects in miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed experiment uses approximately 5 × 5 × 10 mm³ components, an argon atmosphere, thermal imaging, and identical layer thickness and hatch spacing between groups.
The intervention is applicable to miniature AlCrFeNiSi components made in an L-PBF system equipped with in-situ thermal imaging.
Prior HEA studies support an adaptive-scanning and thermal-management mechanism based on machine learning.
EBSD can reveal residual-stress concentrations associated with intergranular cracks.
